question: What primary biological agent contaminates most health care waste materials?
explanation: Body fluids and blood on medical items carry disease-causing germs that present biological hazards. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h1)

question: Why is untreated medical waste a major risk for spreading infections?

options.A: It neutralizes standard hospital disinfectants completely
options.B: It transforms non-pathogenic flora into toxic spores
options.C: It lowers the environmental temperature to foster mold
options.D: It provides organic residues for pathogens to multiply

explanation: Contaminated waste supplies nutrients and moisture that allow harmful germs to grow rapidly. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h1)

question: Used surgical scalpels and hypodermic needles belong to which waste category?
explanation: Any item with a point or edge that can cause punctures or cuts is classified as sharps waste. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h2)

question: Where should you throw away discarded surgical gauze soaked in fresh patient blood?
explanation: Materials soiled with blood or body fluids carry high infection risks and belong in infectious waste containers. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h2)

question: What is the most common way healthcare workers get infected by pathogens on the job?
explanation: Puncture wounds from improperly discarded needles directly introduce bloodborne pathogens into the worker. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h3)

question: How do scavengers and rodents help spread disease from open dump sites?

options.A: They act as mechanical vectors carrying pathogens
options.B: They manufacture synthetic toxins in their bodies
options.C: They convert heavy metals into volatile gases
options.D: They sterilize the waste by consuming bacteria

explanation: Animals foraging through exposed medical refuse physically transport germs into surrounding human settlements. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h3)

question: What dangerous chemicals are released into the air when plastic medical waste is burned in the open?
explanation: Burning plastics at low temperatures in the open produces persistent organic pollutants like dioxins and furans. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h4)

question: How does waste from a poorly managed dumpsite usually contaminate nearby water sources?

options.B: Direct splashing of waste by heavy winds
options.C: Leachate filtering down into underground aquifers
options.D: Rain clouds absorbing toxic vapors from the soil

explanation: Liquid passing through waste collects harmful substances and carries them into groundwater tables and rivers. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h4)

question: At what point in the clinical workflow should medical waste be sorted?
explanation: Sorting waste immediately where it is generated prevents the contamination of non-hazardous materials. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h5)

question: What happens when infectious waste is mistakenly thrown into a general waste bin?

options.A: It automatically neutralizes due to municipal processing
options.B: It contaminates the entire batch and raises infection risks
options.C: It evaporates safely under standard room temperature
options.D: It turns into harmless compost within forty-eight hours

explanation: Mixing hazardous items with regular refuse turns safe trash into an infectious hazard for handlers. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h5)

question: Which machine uses high-pressure steam to sterilize medical instruments and waste?
explanation: Autoclaves apply pressurized steam to destroy microorganisms on infectious materials reliably. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h6)

question: Why must an incinerator have proper emission filters when burning medical waste?

options.A: To increase the speed at which plastic items melt
options.B: To prevent toxic pollutants from escaping into the atmosphere
options.C: To cool down the burnt ash before manual collection
options.D: To convert liquid residue into useful chemical fertilizer

explanation: Emission filters capture hazardous gases and particles, protecting surrounding air quality during incineration. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h6)

question: A nurse notices a safety box for sharps is filled past the recommended fill line. What action should be taken?

options.A: Leave the box open until the end of the night shift
options.B: Press down on the needles with a gloved hand to make space
options.C: Transfer some used needles into an ordinary paper carton
options.D: Close and seal the box immediately for safe disposal

explanation: Safety boxes must never be overfilled; they should be sealed and replaced promptly to avoid needle-stick injuries. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h7)

question: Which task highlights the leadership role of nurses in hospital waste management?

options.A: Supervising ward attendants and enforcing segregation rules
options.B: Operating municipal power plants for clinical incinerators
options.C: Transporting sealed waste trucks to distant regional dumps
options.D: Manufacturing heavy-duty plastic bins for the facility

explanation: Nurses manage ward routines and guide support staff to maintain strict compliance with infection control protocols. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h7)
